## ✨ Highlights

- 🛡️ **A drained BGP member announces nothing, from BIRD's very start**: the configuration janusd hands BIRD now says the `haproxy_*` protocols are down while the node's gate is closed - drained, or HAProxy not healthy. A member back from its update's reboot, or a `bird.conf` applied while it is drained, no longer lets the router hear its route for a moment ([#430](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/430), [BGP](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/bgp.md#a-configuration)).
- ⏸️ **Pause a log target, then resume it**: a **Pause** / **Resume** button on each target's row - on a node's page, the Controller's own logs and the fleet profiles - and `janusctl system log-forwarding pause|resume TARGET`. The secrets stay, and a resumed target goes on from where it stopped, as far as the node kept its lines ([#426](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/426), [Pausing a target](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/log-forwarding.md#pausing-a-target)).
- 🔎 **The Controller's audit names what each entry is about**: *Node edge-1* instead of a hex ID - as it was named then, removed nodes included -, every entry reachable with **Load older**, and filters you can share: account, API token, node, result, kind of action, method, time range, address, text ([#428](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/428)).
- 🧪 **A node on a pre-release changes its apps on that pre-release**: **Change the image** built the newest release instead, and offered to take the node back to it ([#429](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/429)).
- 🖥️ **Choose the CPU model of each Proxmox VE hypervisor's machines**: `x86-64-v2-AES` (the default), `x86-64-v3`, `x86-64-v4`, `host` or a named model, checked against the host's processor. Only `host` or a named model gives HAProxy's TLS 1.3 front AES-GCM - the hints say which model gives what ([#427](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/427), [The CPU model of Proxmox VE machines](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/hypervisors.md#the-cpu-model-of-proxmox-ve-machines)).

## ⚙️ Node

- **BIRD reads the `haproxy_*` protocols as the gate says** ([#430](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/430), fixes [#375](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/375)):
  - The copy of `bird.conf` BIRD reads gets `disabled; /* held down by janusd */` in each `haproxy_*` protocol while the gate is closed - at boot (the drain kept on STATE included), on each gate change and on each apply. BIRD's messages keep your line numbers.
  - Before, BIRD started with them up and janusd took them down about a second later; and a `bird.conf` applied while the node was drained brought them up until the next check, every time - the router heard an update and a withdraw.
  - Opening the gate reconfigures BIRD from your own `bird.conf`: a protocol it disables stays down. A protocol your configuration already disables is left alone.
- **Log forwarding** ([#426](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/426)): a target removed while paused now forgets its place, as a running one did - added again under the same name, it starts from now instead of sending an old backlog.
- **QEMU's guest agent 11.1.3** (extension `qemu-guest-agent`, [#410](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/410)): a maintenance update, nothing changed in qemu-ga itself; the QEMU release's security fixes are all in the emulator, which Janus doesn't ship.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **Audit** ([#428](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/428), fixes [#425](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/425)):
  - Each entry names its subject - a node (its pages' relayed calls included), a pending node, a machine, a cluster, a hypervisor, an account, an API or enrollment token, a sign-on provider - looked up before the request runs, so a deletion still names what it removed. The page links to it while it exists and says *(removed)* once it's gone; entries written before this release are named from the newest entry that did, or from what exists today.
  - `GET /api/audit` takes `before=` (a cursor) and answers `X-Total-Count` and `X-Next-Before`; filters `user`, `via`, `subject`, `result`, `kind`, `method`, `from`/`to`, `client`, `q`; `?facets=1` lists what there is to filter by. The page shows 100 entries at a time and keeps its filters in the address.
  - The log line and the ECS record the Controller ships carry the subject (`janus.audit.subject.kind/id/name`).
  - Still admin only.
- **Changing a pre-release node's image** ([#429](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/429), fixes [#405](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/405)): on a node running a pre-release, **Update › Change the image** builds that pre-release with the chosen apps - or the newest pre-release when a newer one is out - and shows that version's catalog. A node on a release still gets the release, and the pre-release stays out of the update badge and the security badge. The create-a-node form shows the catalog of the version typed in.
- **Proxmox VE: the CPU model per hypervisor** ([#427](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/427), fixes [#372](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/372)):
  - `proxmox.cpu_model` on `POST`/`PATCH`/`GET /api/hypervisors`, the **CPU model its machines get** select on the form, the model on the hypervisor's card. Models without AES-NI, `max` and custom models are refused; the x86-64 levels are checked against the host's processor, and a machine is never created on a host that can't run its model.
  - **What it gives HAProxy**: `x86-64-v2-AES` and `x86-64-v3` have AES-NI but no PCLMULQDQ, and AWS-LC's TLS 1.3 server then prefers ChaCha20 - AES-GCM needs `host` or a named model (Westmere and newer). TLS 1.2, backend TLS and janusd use AES-NI with any of them. `host` ties live migration to identical hosts.
  - Changing the setting restarts nothing: the machines made before show the difference on their card, and **Apply settings** gives them the new model, one clean restart each (a cluster member drained first).
- **Log forwarding**: **Pause** / **Resume** on a target's row ([#426](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/426), fixes [#424](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/424)) - like an edit, saved with the page's **Save**. A paused target shows one badge, *paused*. A node whose forwarding a fleet profile sets is paused through the profile.

## 💻 janusctl

- **`janusctl system log-forwarding pause|resume TARGET`** ([#426](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/426)): flips the target and keeps its secrets; says so when it's already in that state, and names the profile to pause when a Controller profile sets the node's forwarding. `TARGET` completes from the node's targets.

## 🧱 Terraform

- `janus_proxmox_hypervisor.cpu_model`, and `cpu_model` on the `janus_hypervisor` data source ([#427](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/427)).

## 🧪 Tests

- **The in-place cluster update on every build**: `qemu-cluster-upgrade-test` (VRRP, under load, with a member that reverts) and `qemu-cluster-upgrade-bgp-test` (anycast, under load, the router sampled while a drained member reboots) now run in image-build ([#430](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/430)).
- `controller-libvirt-test` updates a cluster of the Controller's own machines in place, between two published releases (opt-in: it needs the internet) ([#430](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/430)).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Proxmox VE machines and TLS 1.3**: the default model, `x86-64-v2-AES`, doesn't bring HAProxy's TLS 1.3 front back to AES-GCM, as v2026.10.28-2's notes said it would - ChaCha20 stays. Set the hypervisor's model to `host` (identical hosts) or a named model, then **Apply settings** on each machine, a cluster's members one at a time, drained.
- **A Proxmox VE machine whose model was set by hand** to a bare `host` or `x86-64-v3` on a hypervisor left at the default now shows a difference on its card. Nothing restarts: set the hypervisor's model to the one you chose.
- **The audit's API answers as before** (an array, 500 entries by default); scripts can read the two new headers to go further back.
